cut.note: a happens-before race detector with three mechanisms and its own test corpus: every thread carries a vector timestamp (a VTS, small-integer VtsID) advanced at synchronisation points so that two events are ordered iff one thread's clock dominates the other's; every memory location carries a shadow value (SVal) recording the read/write clocks at which it was last touched, and a memory-state machine flags an access as a race when it is not ordered after the previous conflicting access; and a lock-order acquisition graph (LAOG) records the order in which locks are taken so a cycle warns of a potential deadlock. The fixtures are the calibration set: each program commits one named error and Helgrind must report it

organs.human_name: libhb_core.c: VtsID (small-int IDs for vector timestamps), SO (synchronisation objects) carrying a VTS, the comment 'the happens-before relationship in concurrent programs'; thread creation, join, lock, unlock and condvar signal transfer clocks
organs.mechanism: each thread has a vector clock mapping every thread to the last event of that thread it has synchronised with; a synchronisation operation (unlock/lock on the same lock, signal/wait, create/join) copies the releasing thread's clock into the acquiring thread's by pointwise maximum; event A happens-before event B iff A's whole vector is <= B's, so two accesses are concurrent (a candidate race) exactly when neither clock dominates the other; VtsIDs intern whole vectors as integers so comparison and reference-counting are cheap
organs.input: the stream of memory and synchronisation events
organs.state: the per-thread and per-SO vector timestamps
assumptions: all inter-thread ordering flows through observable synchronisation primitives, so a race not mediated by one is detectable as unordered (Lamport 1978; the pure happens-before method, no lockset)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: races reported with no false positives from lock discipline alone (unlike Eraser's lockset), at the cost of missing races that a run's schedule happened to order
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: happens-before detection is schedule-dependent (a race not exercised by this interleaving is not reported); vector clocks cost O(threads) per location
organs.human_prior: Lamport 1978 (vector clocks); Flanagan & Freund; the FastTrack lineage
organs.source_boundary: the VTS/SO machinery; MEDIUM because the arithmetic bodies were not read

organs.human_name: libhb_core.c: SVal (a 64-bit shadow per location encoding the read-min and write-min VtsIDs, or NOACCESS); msmcread / msmcwrite (the read/write transitions); zsm shadow-memory with line-Z dictionaries of up to 4 distinct SVals per line
organs.mechanism: each memory word has a shadow value holding the minimal read and write clocks at which it was last accessed (a compressed 'constraint' C(rmin, wmin)); a new read is a race if it is not ordered after the last write; a new write is a race if it is not ordered after the last write or the last read; the transition functions update the shadow to the new access's clocks; shadow memory is stored in cache lines that hold a small dictionary of distinct SVals (most lines have one or two), so the per-word overhead is amortised
organs.input: a memory access with the accessing thread's clock
organs.output: a race report or a state update
assumptions: a location's history is summarised by its last read and last write clocks (FastTrack's insight that the full history is unnecessary); most adjacent words share a shadow, so a dictionary per line compresses it
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: race detection at constant shadow per location rather than a full access history
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: only conflicting accesses are checked; benign races and races the schedule ordered are missed; the 4-SVal line dictionary spills to a LineF when a line is too diverse
organs.source_boundary: the SVal encoding and the msm transitions; MEDIUM because the transition bodies were skimmed

organs.human_name: hg_main.c: univ_laog (sets of Lock*), laog__pre_thread_acquires_lock (1004, 1181, 1258), laog__sanity_check, the lock-order check on each acquisition
organs.mechanism: each time a thread acquires a lock while already holding others, an edge is added from each held lock to the newly acquired one; before adding, the graph is checked for a cycle through the new edge, and a cycle means two lock-acquisition orders that could deadlock under the right schedule; the warning is issued whether or not a deadlock actually happened in this run, so it catches latent lock-order bugs that a single interleaving would not expose
organs.input: lock acquisitions with the current held-set
organs.output: a lock-order graph and cycle warnings
assumptions: a consistent global lock order prevents deadlock, so any cycle in the observed order is a potential deadlock even absent an actual one (the classic lock-hierarchy discipline)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: potential deadlocks found from correct runs; the complement to the go-runtime-deadlock-fixtures detector which fires only on an actual deadlock
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: reports order inversions that the program may in fact serialise by another mechanism (false positives on gate locks); the graph is garbage-collected as locks are destroyed
organs.human_prior: the lock-hierarchy rule; Helgrind's LAOG implementation
organs.source_boundary: the laog functions; MEDIUM because only the hooks were read

pressures.source_evidence: libhb_core.c happens-before + MSM; hg_main.c LAOG; the 259-file test corpus
pressures.condition: an organism observes one execution of a multithreaded program via its memory and synchronisation events; the program may contain a data race or a lock-order inversion that this schedule did not make manifest; the score is detected true errors and false positives on a labelled corpus
pressures.resource_or_constraint: per-thread vector clocks; per-location shadow; a lock-order graph
pressures.failure_condition: a real race or potential deadlock missed, or a benign access flagged
pressures.world_punishes: testing only what the schedule exercised; lockset methods that false-positive on non-lock synchronisation
pressures.world_rewards: happens-before order, per-location conflict shadows, a lock-order graph that fires on inversions not deadlocks
pressures.observable_consequence: true-positive and false-positive counts on the helgrind/tests corpus (tc01_simple_race, hg02_deadlock, tc04_free_lock, locked_vs_unlocked, pth_mempcpy_false_races, ...) where each program's intended verdict is known
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: running every schedule (model checking, infeasible for real programs)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the corpus's labels must match them; a lockset-only detector must false-positive on the happens-before-only fixtures (annotate_hbefore, pth_mempcpy_false_races); a happens-before detector without the LAOG must miss the potential-deadlock fixtures: the corpus is the oracle and shows both gaps
